author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
Thanks Dan — your hypothesis looks exactly right, and on a clean three-way run PE and TAXSIM actually agree to the cent; the only difference is vs TaxAct, and it's the age boundary you flagged.

**Three-way (TAXSIM-35 binary `cdate-20260521`):**

| | PE `page=64` | TAXSIM `page=64` | TaxAct (IT-140) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Schedule M senior modification | $0 | $0 | **$8,000** |
| WV taxable income | 50,585.51 | 50,585.51 | **42,695** |
| WV tax | 1,635.50 | 1,635.50 | **1,284** |

Coding the head as `page=65`, both PE and TAXSIM reproduce TaxAct exactly — $8,000 modification, WV taxable $42,585, tax $1,280.30 (the ~$4 is the spouse's $109 half-of-interest modification). So PE's WV senior-modification logic ([`wv_senior_citizen_disability_deduction_person`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/master/policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/wv/tax/income/subtractions/senior_citizen_disability/wv_senior_citizen_disability_deduction_person.py) — per-person, 65+, capped at that person's own income) matches the form: TaxAct applied the single $8,000 to the income-earning head.

The whole gap is the age input. Per [IRS Pub 501](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p501) ("considered to reach age 65 on the day before the 65th birthday … for 2025, 65 or older if **born before January 2, 1961**"), a Jan-1-1961 birthdate is 65 for TY2025, which is why TaxAct applied the modification. PE and the emulator only ever receive the integer `page`, never a birthdate, so neither can apply that rule — there's nothing to change in PolicyEngine or the emulator here.

**Should the record code `page=65` for a Jan-1-1961 birthdate (per the "born before Jan 2, 1961" rule), to match what you entered in TaxAct?** If so, all three line up.
